title: Inflicting terror, a good way to increase your value
summary: Becoming unpredictable provides a strategic advantage because people feel safe and superior only when they can anticipate your actions. By sending conflicting signals, you create distress, confusion, and panic, forcing opponents to blunder and lose their ability to think straight. Depending on the target, unpredictability can instill terror or generate intense interest and attention.
example: Bobby Fischer used erratic behavior, late arrivals, complaints, and novel chess moves to break Boris Spassky's rhythm and force blunders.
Filippo used series of confusions to see under the skins of his courtiers.
A war general used repetitive tactics to fool the enemy and buy time for reinforcements.
Pablo Picasso used unpredictability of actions on co-workers.
reversal: Predictability increases a sense of safety and security around people.
When you lack sufficient power, being unpredictable can backfire by causing you to be labeled as deceptive or psychic, reducing your value.
You must carefully time when to be predictable versus unpredictable to protect your reputation.
